microtheory.name: humanities_foundation
microtheory.definition: Foundational vocabulary for the humanities as a class — disciplines studying meaning, expression, value, and tradition through interpretation rather than measurement. Where the social sciences ask about regularities + causes across populations, the humanities ask what a text, ritual, performance, image, or practice MEANS, in its own terms and in relation to a tradition. This Mt names the methodological + conceptual machinery shared across literature, performance_arts, religion_theology, and gastronomy as a cultural-craft tradition — interpretation + hermeneutics, canon + genre + periodization, primary + secondary sources, exegesis + critical theory, narrative + transmission. The 4 humanities island Mts inherit from this; cortex's compositional_reuse can now see the cluster as a tree. Distinct from language_foundation (the units of language) and pragmatics_linguistics (the use of language). This is the broader interpretive + traditional foundation.

concepts.name: interpretation
concepts.definition: The activity of making meaning explicit from a text, performance, ritual, image, or practice — never a single right answer, always a reading from a stance. Substrate analogue: substrate's frame-dependent reading of an input under its current Mt configuration.

concepts.name: hermeneutics
concepts.definition: The theory + art of interpretation. Schleiermacher's grammatical + psychological circles, Dilthey's verstehen, Heidegger's pre-understanding, Gadamer's fusion of horizons, Ricoeur's hermeneutics of suspicion + recovery. Substrate analogue: substrate's interpretive cortex with its own pre-Mt baggage.

concepts.name: hermeneutic_circle
concepts.definition: Understanding the whole requires understanding the parts; understanding the parts requires understanding the whole. Interpretation moves circularly, not linearly. Substrate analogue: substrate's iterative cortex assessment.

concepts.name: exegesis
concepts.definition: Close interpretive reading drawing out a text's intended or possible meanings, traditionally of scripture or canonical works. Distinguished from eisegesis (reading-IN unsupported meaning). Substrate analogue: substrate's grounded extraction of structure from a single source.

concepts.name: critical_theory
concepts.definition: Frankfurt School + descendants — Adorno, Horkheimer, Benjamin, Marcuse, Habermas. Also broader post-1968 critical traditions: structuralism, post-structuralism, deconstruction (Derrida), Foucault, postcolonial (Said, Spivak, Bhabha), feminist, queer, ecocritical. Reading texts/practices to surface ideology, power, exclusion. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspection of its own frozen Mts as a source of bias.

concepts.name: canonization
concepts.definition: The historical process by which certain works/traditions become 'the canon' — required reading, central works, normative reference points. Always contested; canon-formation is a power move. Substrate analogue: substrate's promotion of certain Concepts to foundational status.

concepts.name: tradition
concepts.definition: A line of transmitted practice + interpretation that constitutes a discipline, religion, art form, craft. MacIntyre: a tradition is an extended argument about the goods constitutive of that tradition. Substrate analogue: the substrate's evolving Mt lineage.

concepts.name: transmission
concepts.definition: How a tradition's content moves across generations + media — manuscript, print, oral, performance, ritual, apprenticeship. Loss, drift, reinterpretation are intrinsic. Substrate analogue: substrate save/load + cross-instance Mt transfer.

concepts.name: canon
concepts.definition: The set of works/practices considered authoritative within a tradition. Western literary canon, biblical canon, ragas in Indian classical music, the haute cuisine repertoire. Substrate analogue: substrate's set of frozen reference Mts.

concepts.name: periodization
concepts.definition: Division of cultural history into named periods — Classical, Medieval, Renaissance, Romantic, Modernist, Postmodern. A heuristic, not a fact; periods overlap + are contested. Substrate analogue: substrate's epoch labels on its own developmental trajectory.

concepts.name: genre
concepts.definition: A conventional kind — epic, lyric, tragedy, novel, sonata, raga, ritual form, cuisine. Genres set expectations that works fulfill, subvert, or hybridise. Substrate analogue: substrate's named Mt categories scaffolding new instances.

concepts.name: primary_source
concepts.definition: An original document, artifact, work, or testimony from the period or context studied. Substrate analogue: substrate's direct sensor trace.

concepts.name: secondary_source
concepts.definition: A scholarly work interpreting + commenting on primary sources. Substrate analogue: substrate's derived Mt summary of a primary trace.

concepts.name: tertiary_source
concepts.definition: Reference works — encyclopedias, handbooks — synthesising secondary literature. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-altitude foundation Mts compressing many secondary Mts.

concepts.name: philology
concepts.definition: Historical + comparative study of texts in their linguistic + cultural context. Manuscript traditions, textual criticism, edition. Substrate analogue: substrate's careful reconstruction of a Concept's original sense across versions.

concepts.name: narrative
concepts.definition: An ordered telling of events with selection, perspective, voice, and (usually) point. The basic form of cultural meaning-making. Substrate analogue: substrate's sequential trace as the unit of self-explanation.

concepts.name: rhetoric
concepts.definition: The art of effective communication — Aristotle's ethos/pathos/logos; classical figures + tropes; persuasion's structure. Substrate analogue: substrate's selection of expression strategy under audience model.

concepts.name: figurative_language
concepts.definition: Metaphor, metonymy, simile, irony, synecdoche, allegory, symbol. Non-literal meaning carries the bulk of cultural weight. Substrate analogue: substrate's analogical-transfer machinery.

concepts.name: intertextuality
concepts.definition: Kristeva, Barthes. Texts refer to + transform other texts; every text is a tissue of quotations + echoes. Substrate analogue: substrate's cross-Mt reference graph.

concepts.name: aesthetic_value
concepts.definition: Value of an object/experience as art — beauty, sublimity, expressiveness, formal coherence, originality. Contested ground (Kant, Hegel, Dewey, Danto, Dickie). Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-drive applied to expressive structures.

concepts.name: sacred
concepts.definition: Eliade, Otto. A category of objects, places, times, persons set apart as ultimate, transcendent, non-mundane. The opposite of profane. Substrate analogue: substrate's frozen-most-protected Mts.

concepts.name: ritual
concepts.definition: Patterned, repeated, prescribed action carrying meaning beyond instrumental function. Religious, civic, life-cycle, performative. Turner, van Gennep. Substrate analogue: substrate's stable enacted patterns marking transitions.

concepts.name: authorship
concepts.definition: Attribution of a work to a creator. Pre-modern + post-Barthes ('death of the author') destabilisations of the unitary author. Substrate analogue: substrate's provenance edges on Concepts.

concepts.name: reception
concepts.definition: Jauss, Iser, Fish. How a work is received, read, performed, used by audiences across time + context — meaning is not only in the work but in the encounter. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ pattern on re-encountering a Mt under a new frame.

rules.name: interpretation_is_framed_not_arbitrary
rules.head: the substrate is offered competing readings of a work
rules.body: interpretations are constrained by text, tradition, context, plausibility — not all readings are equal — but no single reading exhausts meaning. Substrate must avoid both 'one true reading' + 'anything goes'.

rules.name: hermeneutic_circle_requires_iteration
rules.head: the substrate must understand a work
rules.body: first pass uses pre-understanding; understanding parts revises the whole; revised whole revises parts. Substrate iterates rather than parsing once + stopping.

rules.name: canon_is_contested_not_natural
rules.head: the substrate accepts a list as 'the canon' of a tradition
rules.body: canonization is a historical process with politics + exclusion; flagging that does not dissolve the canon, but the substrate should never report it as natural fact.

rules.name: primary_secondary_distinction_governs_evidence
rules.head: the substrate makes a claim about a tradition
rules.body: weight + warrant rest on primary sources where possible; secondary sources mediate + may misrepresent.

rules.name: tradition_carries_an_internal_argument
rules.head: the substrate observes a discipline disagreeing with itself
rules.body: internal argument about the goods constitutive of the tradition is the SIGN of a living tradition, not its failure. MacIntyre.

rules.name: figurative_meaning_is_not_decorative
rules.head: the substrate encounters metaphor in a humanities source
rules.body: metaphor + figurative structure often carry the central content, not decoration; literalising loses the meaning.
